model: 40VM Series VRF BACnet Interface 40VM900052A (outdoor header unit objects)
applies_to: Outdoor header (and follower) units of Carrier 40VM series VRF systems connected to the 40VM900052A BACnet Interface.
summary: Through the 40VM900052A interface, each VRF outdoor header unit appears as its own BACnet device with 20 objects: ambient and discharge temperatures, pressures, compressor and fan speeds, malfunction code, on/off, alarm and mode status, plus system-wide multistate outputs (all off, energy limit, fan speed at zero capacity, dry contact 4 settings) that act on every indoor unit of that system. Follower units show only the 13 inputs.
default_device_instance: NNNPAAA (virtual network number, XYE port, unit address)
notes: Each outdoor unit is a separate BACnet device; outdoor unit addresses are 96-127 in the NNNPAAA device ID rule.
Follower outdoor units have the same 13 input objects (AI 1-10, BI 1-2, MI 1) and no outputs.

The SYS_MO objects are group commands for all indoor units of that refrigerant system and only work on the header unit. MO 11-16 are write-only (the value cannot be read back); MO 10 is readable and writable. MO 14-16 state texts are temperature and time steps, not repeated here.
Access is inferred: inputs read-only, outputs writable.

source.title: 40VM Series VRF System BACnet Interface Installation and Operation Manual, Part Number 40VM900052A (Table 69, BACnet Object List of Outdoor Header Unit)

points.name: ODU_MI_ModeStatus
points.states: 1=Turn Off, 2=Fan, 3=Cooling, 4=Heating, 5=Force to Cool, 6=Main Cooling, 7=Main Heating, 8=Force to Heat

points.name: SYS_MO_AllCoolStopFan
points.description: Indoor fan speed when cooling capacity is 0 (all units)

points.name: SYS_MO_AllHeatStopFan
points.description: Indoor fan speed when heating capacity is 0 (all units)

points.name: SYS_MO_AllDryContact4On
points.description: Dry contact 4 on temperature difference (all units)

points.name: SYS_MO_AllDryContact4Off
points.description: Dry contact 4 off temperature difference (all units)

integration.summary: Read outdoor unit status and diagnostics from the header unit device; the SYS_MO outputs give group commands such as turning off all indoor units of the system (MO 11) or an energy limit level (MO 10).

minimum_points.name: SYS_MO_AllTurnOff
minimum_points.why: Group command: turn off/on all indoor units

minimum_points.name: SYS_MO_AllEnergyLimit
minimum_points.why: System energy limit level (No Limit, Level 1-5)

setup: Default IP address of the interface is 192.168.1.8; change it in the web interface.
Indoor unit addresses are 0-95 and outdoor units 96-127 on each XYE port.
Each outdoor unit system needs a unique network address 0-7, set with the rotary encoder on the outdoor unit.
gotchas: MO 11-16 are write-only group commands; reading them does not reflect indoor unit state.
Group commands act on every indoor unit of the refrigerant system served by that header unit.
After writing the energy limit (MO 10), the interface must keep talking to the outdoor unit for at least 1 minute or the limit setting is reported invalid.
